card.name: Articles before a drug class name
card.fires_on: The article "a" or "an" (and sometimes the start of "anthracycline") right before a drug or drug class name, often after "with" or "or". Also fires on the space after a drug name before its dose.

modes.label: Article before drug class
modes.description: "a" or "an" after "with", "or" or a comma, introducing a drug class such as anthracycline or anti-inflammatory agent.
modes.example: concurrent prophylactic treatment with colchicine or<< an>> anti-inflammatory agent is recommended

modes.label: Inside anthracycline
modes.description: The middle piece of the word anthracycline in cardiac-risk warnings.

modes.label: Space after drug name
modes.description: The gap right after a drug name, just before its mg dose.
modes.example: Administer trastuzumab<< >>6 mg/kg intravenously as soon

card.plain: It fires on small words like "a" or "an" that come just before a drug or drug class is named.
